reason: The text demonstrates the opposite of the stated claim. God shows profound empathy for the common people of Nineveh (non-Israelites), not just Hebrew leaders. When the people of Nineveh repent, God shows mercy and does not destroy them (Jonah 3:10). Most significantly, at the text's conclusion (Jonah 4:10-11), God explicitly rebukes Jonah (a Hebrew prophet/leader) for lacking compassion, arguing that He cannot destroy Nineveh because of the 'many people' who cannot discern right from left, plus the animals. God's concern is demonstrated to extend to the vulnerable masses and even animals, while the text actually criticizes a Hebrew spiritual leader for his lack of empathy. The narrative inverts the claim entirely.
